Well, thanks for mentioning Greg. As you referenced, I do serve on the intelligence committee. We had a rare open source hearing this week in Washington DC that was on Tuesday. So the public got to see the FBI director and the CIA director. And that gave me an opportunity to talk about the FISA abuses that have gone on with the FBI. And listen, I'm someone that's been very supportive of federal law enforcement and the FBI. However, what happened with FISA needed to be brought to light and the abuses that happened there. And so on Tuesday, we talked about Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which, as you referenced, permits the government to conduct targeted surveillance of foreign persons located outside of the US. And what it included was FBI agents and personnel, you know, looking at domestic activities of people, not what the law is supposed to be looking at, which is people outside of the United States that have foreign terrorist ties. They were looking at things like health care and fraud and bribery and public corruption. And those things are fine, but it shouldn't be done within FISA. And this opinion issued last year takes the FBI to task. And so I might question this week, really highlighted those abuses and the process and what needs to be done. And so the FBI Director, you know, had an opportunity to kind of defend the FBI there and talk about the process and put in place to change that, the new protocols have been put in place. And those sound good, but we're going to have to stay on the FBI, you know, to make sure that this gets implemented the right way, that there's no more abuses. And as we saw with um, crossfire hurricane that went after president Trump. Uh, the FBI abused the process there. And so we have an obligation and responsibility to hold the FBI accountable.
